Subject: Recap: discovery call — latency/throughput pain + next steps

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap so we’re all aligned and have clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

TL;DR
- Primary pain: intermittent latency spikes (p95 often >700–800ms) causing UI timeouts during peak usage.
- Goal: sub-300ms p95 for typical user flows (summarization/generation up to ~256 tokens) and sustained throughput to support 150–200 concurrent requests at peak.
- Constraint: must run in Acme’s Azure subscription (VNet + private endpoints) and meet SOC2 requirements for logging/audit.

What we discussed
- Current prod: single-region hosted model (3rd-party) with occasional CPU/GPU contention. Peak observed concurrency ~120 QPS; typical request size ~150–300 tokens.
- Desired SLOs: p50 ~50–100ms, p95 <=300ms (generation up to 256 tokens). Throughput target 150 req/s sustained with burst to 250 for short windows.
- Tolerances: can accept higher latency for longer outputs (>512 tokens) and for non-critical background jobs.

Model & quality notes
- You prefer a 7B–13B class base model with custom fine-tuning for your summarization prompts. Embedding workloads are separate — not in-scope for this initial deployment.
- Reducing model size or quantizing are acceptable if inference quality stays within your eval pass rates.

Next steps (action items)
1) Acme -> share a short load trace (CSV) and 30-day traffic profile (you mentioned you’d send this).
2) Redwood SEs (Sean & Dev) will prepare a recommended topology and SLO runbook + a perf plan for an on-site test in your Azure tenant.
3) Lauren will follow up on timeline and questions on procurement / committed capacity.

Attachments referenced: acme-load-trace.csv (you mentioned), placeholder for Redwood TDR doc.

Thanks — I’ll let Sean and Dev follow up with the technical deep-dive.

—

Subject: Technical deep-dive recap & recommended deployment topology (based on your trace)

Alex / Priya — thanks for the trace. Below is a concise technical recommendation and the perf plan we’ll use for the Azure private deployment. I’ve attached a short PDF (redwood-tdr-20260304.pdf) with diagrams and cost/latency projections.

Summary of goals we’ll optimize for
- p95 <= 300ms for generation requests up to 256 tokens
- Sustained throughput: 150 req/s; burst to 250 req/s for short windows
- SOC2-compatible logging and audit trail; private-networking in Azure VNet

Key observations from your trace
- Peak bursts to 220 QPS for ~2–10 minute windows
- Median request length ~180 tokens; tail up to ~600 tokens

Recommended topology (Azure, private):
- Deployment: Redwood Private control plane + runtime deployed into Acme Azure subscription (Central US) using a dedicated resource group and VNet + private endpoints.
- Serving nodes: start with a 2-node pool of A100-style GPU instances (or equivalent vGPU config) in a warm pool for fast cold-starts; target ~2x for redundancy.
- Model variants: primary = 13B quantized to int8 (if eval pass) or 7B int8 as fallback. Keep a smaller 3B variant for ultra-low-cost fallback routing.
- Autoscaling & routing: workload-aware autoscaler with continuous batching; scale-up policy on sustained queue length and p95 breach; routing policy to prefer local region then failover to Redwood-hosted Dedicated pool as a last resort.
- Caching: prefix / KV cache for repeated prompts; request-level response caching for deterministic prompts.

Performance & SLO tuning
- Batching: tune batching window to ~6–10ms for latency-sensitive flows (trade-off between latency and throughput).
- Target GPU utilization: 60–80% for cost efficiency while keeping headroom for bursts.
- Observability: per-request token-level latency breadcrumbs, p50/p95/p99 dashboards, and alerting on sustained p95 > 300ms.

Test plan (what we’ll run in your tenant)
1) Baseline run: single-node cold start + steady-state 120 QPS, 180-token median, measure p50/p95/p99.
2) Burst test: reproduce 220 QPS bursts for 10 minutes; observe scaling and p95.
3) Long-tail test: run 5% requests at 600 tokens to validate tail behavior.
4) Fallback routing validation: simulate primary model OOM and confirm routing to 3B variant and preserved SLA for availability (but degraded quality).

Data/Security notes
- We’ll integrate with your KMS for key material; logs will be pushed to your Log Analytics workspace behind private endpoints.
- SOC2 evidence: we can provide audit artifacts (config snapshots, access logs) as part of the procurement pack.

Attachments: redwood-tdr-20260304.pdf (topology diagrams, perf projections)

Next steps
- Sean/Dev: schedule a 90-minute on-site perf run in your tenant (can be remote) — propose Wed 2026-03-11 or Thu 2026-03-12.
- Acme: confirm preferred model family (7B vs 13B), and grant a service principal with limited rights for the perf run.
- Lauren/Marissa: move procurement timeline forward and confirm whether committed capacity is on the table.

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the attachment.

Thanks Alex / Priya — adding a short engineering checklist so the perf run is low friction. Copying Sean for the perf schedule.

Engineering checklist for Azure perf run
- Service principal with Contributor on the resource group (we’ll scope down post-validation).
- VNet/subnet and route table details + any NSG rules we should be aware of.
- Log Analytics workspace ID & storage account for audit logs.
- Optional: sample prompts + 1k representative requests (we’ll replay for determinism).

Quick notes on tuning knobs we’ll exercise during the run
- Quantization profile: int8 vs fp16 latency/quality tradeoffs tested head-to-head.
- Batching window: 2ms / 6ms / 10ms profiles to find the best latency/throughput sweet spot.
- KV cache TTLs: tune to maximize hit rates for repeated prompts without stale outputs.

I’ve attached a small test harness and perf script stub (see redwood-tdr-20260304.pdf for links) and will share the exact load commands once we confirm the date.

If Wed 3/11 09:00–10:30 PT works we’ll block time; otherwise propose Thu 3/12 same slot.
